problem: Alice has two email accounts, $A$ and $B.$ In account $A,$ she received $24$ emails of which $5$ are spam. In the account $B,$ she received $18$ emails of which $2$ are spam. What is the probability that a randomly selected email in either account is spam?

feedback.problem: A gas station offers two types of gasoline, regular and premium. On a certain day, of the $43$ customers who bought regular gas, $23$ paid with a credit card. On the same day, of the $38$ customers that bought premium gas, $31$ of them paid with a credit card. What is the probability of a randomly selected customer paying with a credit card?
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be the event that the chosen person paid with a credit card, and let $R$ be the event that the person bought regular gas. Then ${R}^{′}$ is the event that the person bought premium gas.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected person paid with a credit card, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
P(C)=P(C\cap R)+P(C\cap {R}^{′})
$$

To calculate $P(C\cap R),$ we take the number of people who bought regular gas and paid with a credit card $(23)$ and divide by the total number of customers on that day $(43+38=81).$ So, we have

$$
P(C\cap R)=\frac{23}{81}.
$$

Similarly, to calculate $P(C\cap {R}^{′}),$ we take the number of people who bought premium gas and paid with a credit card $(31)$ and divide by the total number of customers on that day $(81).$ So, we have

$$
P(C\cap {R}^{′})=\frac{31}{81}.
$$

Finally, substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected person paid with a credit card is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(C) & =P(C\cap R)+P(C\cap {R}^{′}) \\  & =\frac{23}{81}+\frac{31}{81} \\  & =\frac{54}{81} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
